new_statements.relation_note: Transcription conventions give vowel-symbol equivalences, the stress-marking convention and the non-phonemic-stress remark; nothing on tone seen in snippets.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-level: for all Lumi Subdistrict languages recorded (including Aiku = Yangum), Laycock treats stress as non-phonemic and by default on the first syllable whose vowel is not schwa; he writes a stress mark only where stress falls elsewhere. In the published 46-item Aiku list one form carries such a mark (yimán 'breast'), i.e. default first-full-vowel stress with occasional lexical deviations.
new_statements.exceptions: Forms whose stress is not on the first non-schwa syllable are marked individually in the wordlists (Aiku: yimán 'breast' in the TransNewGuinea transcription of this list).
new_statements.identity_note: The article is Laycock's 1967 survey of the Lumi Subdistrict languages; 'Aiku (Menandon, Minendon, Monanda, Monandu, Umbrak-Aiku): (a) 790 (b) Monandin, Sengi, Suau, Womerau (E. Palei CD), Yirkin (W. Palei CD) (c) NR (d) Nuku 7/67' is the entry for what is now Yangum Mon [ymo] (Monandin/Wumerau = ymo villages per the 2006 ISO request) plus the other Yangum/Ambrak varieties. The stress sentence is a blanket statement in the transcription conventions covering ALL languages in the paper ('any of these languages'), not an Aiku-specific analysis; the Aiku wordlist in the same paper (as reproduced on TransNewGuinea) applies the convention (one marked form, yimán 'breast').
